headline: Kodiak deal narrows GAAP loss, adjusted EPS turns positive
summary_short: QXO's Q2 2026 net sales rose 87.6% q/q to $3,246M as Kodiak Building Partners contributed $595M, narrowing the GAAP operating loss to $42M and net loss to $55M (-$0.14/share), while Adjusted EBITDA rose to $272M and Adjusted Diluted EPS turned positive at $0.08.
summary_long: Q2 2026 net sales rose 87.6% q/q to $3,246M, including $595M from Kodiak Building Partners (acquired April 1). GAAP gross margin expanded to 24.7% (from 21.1% y/y), though Adjusted Gross Margin slipped to 24.7% from 25.3% after excluding a 2025 inventory step-up charge. Operating loss narrowed to $42M from $251.9M q/q as revenue growth outpaced higher SG&A, depreciation and amortization. GAAP net loss was $55M (-$0.14/share); Adjusted Net Income was $130M and Adjusted Diluted EPS was $0.08, down from $0.11 y/y on share dilution (911.8M vs 702.0M weighted diluted shares). Cash fell to $2,774M; long-term debt rose to $6,029M after $3.0B in Senior Notes funded the TopBuild acquisition, which closed July 1. No numeric forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by the addition of Kodiak Building Partners, which contributed $595 million following its April 1, 2026 acquisition, on top of underlying roofing and building-products demand.

GAAP gross margin rose to 24.7% from 21.1% y/y, but the company's own reconciliation shows this is fully explained by an $80M inventory fair-value step-up charge recognized in Q2 2025; Adjusted Gross Margin actually slipped to 24.7% from 25.3%.

Operating loss narrowed q/q as revenue nearly doubled to $3,246M and gross profit rose to $803M, outpacing higher SG&A, depreciation and amortization from the larger consolidated (Kodiak-inclusive) base.
Narrowed q/q on the same operating improvement, partly offset by wider net interest expense ($38M vs $30M y/y) from additional Senior Notes issued ahead of the TopBuild acquisition close.
Rose to $272M from $204M y/y on consolidated growth including Kodiak, though the company's own reconciliation shows Adjusted EBITDA Margin compressed to 8.4% from 10.7%.
Declined to $0.08 from $0.11 y/y despite higher Adjusted Net Income ($130M vs $109M) because adjusted diluted weighted-average shares rose to 911.8M from 702.0M, outpacing income growth.
Increased to fund the pending TopBuild Corp. acquisition: $3.0 billion of Senior Notes (6.500% due 2031, 6.875% due 2034) were issued with proceeds held in escrow pending the deal's close.

CEO Brad Jacobs framed results as reflecting current market conditions while highlighting Kodiak's contribution; following the TopBuild acquisition's July 1 close, QXO says it is now North America's second-largest publicly traded building products distributor, targeting more than double EBITDA by 2030 and $50 billion in revenue within the decade.
